reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is transforming observational noise into structured probabilistic models. Paget's five-grade classification forms a finite support for a random variable. By treating each grade as an event, we can estimate transition probabilities between states using maximum likelihood. This bridges frequentist counting with Bayesian updating: prior beliefs about grade distributions are refined as new data arrive. The derived kernel handles heteroscedasticity—unequal variances across categories—by weighting each observation inversely proportional to its estimated variance. Crucially, this prevents overfitting to rare events while maintaining power for common ones. Failure occurs when underlying dynamics are non-stationary, violating ergodicity. To detect this, monitor the Kullback-Leibler divergence between successive posterior distributions; a sudden spike indicates concept drift.
